evidence: The hunk lists Statuses ['in_progress'] straight from Store.ListIssues with no filterWorkableIssues call, while the doc comment claims the command shares lit ready's orphan definition; containers with derived in_progress state would slip through. The agent added the filter plus TestRunOrphanedExcludesContainerEpics.
guidance_note: When a new command claims to reuse an existing pipeline's definition, reuse that pipeline's whole selection chain (list + filterWorkableIssues + annotate), not just its threshold constant.

evidence: The hunk only adds a new constant, so the packet cannot show the pre-PR ready threshold; the agent says 6h shipped earlier in 6e3b1ab, which the packet neither confirms nor contradicts. The stale '24h+' doc on the Orphaned annotation kind was real, and the agent fixed that while rejecting the revert.
guidance_note: When extracting a constant, grep for prose that restates its value (doc comments, annotation docs) and update it in the same commit.

evidence: The original tests covered JSON, ordering, and the empty case, but not --assignee or epic exclusion; the agent added TestRunOrphanedAssigneeFilter and TestRunOrphanedExcludesContainerEpics.
guidance_note: Write one test per flag and per selection rule a new command introduces before opening the PR.

The threshold finding was half wrong: the revert was refused on a claimed prior master commit, and the stale doc it pointed at was fixed.

narrative: Single round, single comment-accuracy nit, fixed in a1d2b97. Nothing fix-caused.

evidence: The new doc's related-issues bullets used a label prefix instead of the id-first form the reviewer cited from agent-native-guidance-proposal.md; the agent rewrote both bullets in 4429439.
guidance_note: When adding a design doc, copy the header and related-issues shape from an existing sibling doc.

'The next-next ticket' is colloquial in the worked example; the agent replaced it with 'the ticket after next' in 4429439.

narrative: Doc-only PR, one round of three style findings. Two were accepted, one was refused as preference. Nothing fix-caused.

evidence: open(path, errors='replace') with no encoding uses the locale default; the agent pinned encoding='utf-8' on this read and swept all three write sites in 8c4bbf6.
guidance_note: Pin encoding='utf-8' on every open() in a new Python script at write time.

evidence: The hardcoded '-Users-bmf-code-links-issue-tracker' fails on any other clone path, and the agent's derive-from-repo-root fix beats the reviewer's single-dir autodetect. But the agent asserted the encoding is 'just / -> -' and verified it only on a path with no other punctuation, which #91/F2 then flagged.
guidance_note: When reproducing another tool's encoding, check it against a real sample with punctuation (underscores, dots) rather than only the one path that motivated the change.

evidence: truncate() emits an ellipsis and the writers opened files with the locale default; all three writers got encoding='utf-8' in 8c4bbf6 alongside F1.
guidance_note: Pin encoding='utf-8' on every open() in a new Python script at write time.

narrative: One round on the session-analysis script; F1 and F3 were the same encoding gap and the agent swept every open() site at once. F2's fix replaced a machine-specific constant with a derived one, but its asserted '/ -> -' encoding rule drew a follow-up finding in #91.
guidance_observations: Bundling F1 and F3 into one sweep of every open() site is the right pattern: fix the class, not the flagged line.

evidence: The loop assigns turn['thinking'] / turn['text'] = truncate(...) per content item, so a message with several text blocks keeps only the last. The PR was closed as misnamed, and the thread was never answered or carried forward; #92 does not contain this file.
guidance_note: When a parser walks a list of content blocks, accumulate them instead of assigning a scalar per item.

evidence: DEFAULT_PROJECT = str(REPO_ROOT).replace('/', '-') is the #90/F2 fix, and it encodes only one separator. The Windows framing is weak for this tool. Outside the packet, Claude Code project dirs also map '_' to '-' (promptctl_laws becomes promptctl-laws), so the rule fails on POSIX too.
guidance_note: When reproducing another tool's encoding, check it against a real sample with punctuation (underscores, dots) rather than only the one path that motivated the change.

narrative: This was a multi-topic branch, closed as misnamed and reopened as #92 with only the prompt-field work. Both findings were on the session-analysis script already merged in #90, and neither got a reply. F2 is a direct consequence of the #90/F2 fix's under-checked encoding rule.
guidance_observations: Closing a PR orphaned two open review threads on code already on master; findings on a closed PR should be moved to a ticket, not dropped.
The branch carried already-merged work from #90, which re-exposed that code to review under the wrong PR.

evidence: The PR's own ALTERs backtick-quoted `prompt` because it is reserved in Dolt, yet CREATE used it bare. Renaming to agent_prompt removes the collision at every site; 14fd5ea shows every SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE updated plus a probe-gated RENAME.
guidance_note: When a migration has to quote an identifier, apply that quoting (or rename) at every site the identifier appears, starting with CREATE TABLE.

evidence: The probe-gated RENAME exists only because of the F1 fix (14fd5ea); its comment claims idempotence 'across fresh / migrated / pre-rename' states. A both-columns workspace would fail the rename, but no code path in the packet produces one, so the risk is hypothetical. The thread was left unanswered at merge.
guidance_note: When writing a state-gated migration, list every column state it can meet (neither, old, new, both) and state which ones are reachable before claiming idempotence in a comment.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive: 14fd5ea touched only store files and schema.go, and the followup --prompt flag came in the original PR. The packet does not show the usage string, so whether it omits --prompt (and also the optional --description) cannot be confirmed. The thread got no reply.
guidance_note: When adding a flag to a command, update its usage/error string in the same edit.

narrative: Round 0 caught the unquoted reserved column, and the agent fixed it with a rename plus a probe-gated migration. Round 1 flagged a both-columns edge case in that new migration, which is fix-caused but hypothetical. It also flagged a usage-string omission from the original PR. Neither round-1 thread got a reply before merge.
guidance_observations: Two round-1 threads were left unresolved and unanswered at merge; every thread should get a fix or a written refusal.

evidence: The guidance said '(1-2 words)' while giving `dep-rm-relation-not-found` (five segments) as an example, which is a real contradiction. Softening to 'ideally' was the wrong cure; dropping the long example was the right one. The later #98 quickstart lists only 'refactor' and 'field-history', so the example was removed after all.
guidance_note: Check every example in guidance text against the rule it illustrates before committing.

evidence: The help text is guidance whose whole purpose is to push agents toward 1-2 word slugs; validation allowing more does not make the guidance wrong, and 'ideally' would weaken the PR's intent.

narrative: Two-line guidance PR. Both findings proposed softening '1-2 words', which goes against the PR's intent and was correctly refused. But F1 also pointed at a real contradiction, a five-segment example, and that was dismissed along with the bad cure.
guidance_observations: Rejecting a reviewer's cure should not also discard its diagnosis; F1's contradictory example was real and was fixed only later, in #98.

evidence: commandRegistrar.stderr was set but readyRun captured the stderr parameter directly; routing readyRun through r.stderr makes the registrar the one holder of the writers, which is what the struct comment claims.
guidance_note: When introducing a context-carrying struct, grep the closures that build from it for direct captures of the same values.

narrative: Registry refactor, one round with one unused-field finding, fixed in 91f3789. Nothing fix-caused.

evidence: withMutation called commitWorkingSetOnce without commitWorkingSet's trim/default. Hoisting normalization into commitWorkingSetOnce (3196592) fixed the message drift but left withMutation duplicating the retry wrapper. The reviewer's alternative, 'just call s.commitWorkingSet', would have removed both, and the agent adopted exactly that in round 2 for F7.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one behavior two parallel paths disagree on, collapse the duplicate path rather than syncing the one flagged behavior.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: 3196592 touched only commit_lock.go, and the ranking rework is separate new work added after round 0. LiveRankInversions was exported while returning unexported []rankInversion with only in-package callers; it was renamed to liveRankInversions in d9ea9a2.
guidance_note: Export a method only when it has a caller outside the package; default new helpers to lowercase.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: this comment is in the ranking rework, not in 3196592. The comment named liveRankInversions while the function was LiveRankInversions, so the mismatch was real; the F2 rename in d9ea9a2 resolved it.

The flag is a false positive: rowQueryer is part of the ranking rework, not 3196592. 'Queryer' is an established Go spelling (e.g. sqlx.Queryer), so it is not a typo, and the name describes the QueryContext surface exactly.

The flag is a false positive: liveIssueIDs came from the ranking rework, not 3196592. The doc said 'non-deleted' while ListIssues excludes archived rows by default, a real doc/behavior mismatch. The agent kept the behavior (archived is not actionable) and fixed the comment in d9ea9a2, which is the sound choice.
guidance_note: When a doc comment enumerates a filter's exclusions, read the defaults of the call it wraps and list them all.

evidence: The flag is a false positive: d9ea9a2 only renamed and edited comments, and the pre-lock snapshot came from the earlier ranking rework. The agent argued moving liveIssueIDs inside the closure changes nothing because it reads s.db. But the commit lock serializes lit writers, so a snapshot taken under the lock cannot be invalidated by another lit mutation. The move is cheap and narrows the window, though impact on a repair command is low.
guidance_note: When a read must stay consistent with a following locked write, take the read inside the lock that serializes writers, even if it uses a different connection.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT d9ea9a2 is incidental (anchoring at head); the real cause is F1's fix. F1 diagnosed withMutation as a second path into commitWorkingSetOnce, and 3196592 synced only the trim rule, leaving the inline retryTransientManifestReadOnly. 6833bf7 then did what F1 had offered: call s.commitWorkingSet, which is safe because the lock is re-entrant.
guidance_note: When a reviewer flags one behavior two parallel paths disagree on, collapse the duplicate path rather than syncing the one flagged behavior.

narrative: F1 found withMutation diverging from commitWorkingSet. The agent synced only the message normalization, so round 2 had to flag the duplicated retry wrapper (F7), and the agent then took the reviewer's original 'just call commitWorkingSet' suggestion. Round 1's four findings are on rank-inversion work added after round 0, not on the named fix commit. F6's pushback rested on a flawed race argument. Rounds 1 and 2 were triggered by other new pushes, so none is wholly avoidable, but F7 was.
guidance_observations: The PR grew new scope (the rank-inversion rework) mid-review, which produced a whole extra round of findings unrelated to round 0.
The agent's round-2 fix for F7 was the reviewer's round-0 alternative; picking the structural option first would have saved a finding.

evidence: ApplyUpdate always ends with s.UpdateIssue(ctx, id, in.Fields), which by the code's own comment does a fresh GetIssue, so a status-only update re-reads after the transitions commit. A read failure then reports an error for an applied change. The PR merged at 12:09:37, before the review posted at 12:09:56.
guidance_note: When unifying paths, check that the unified path preserves each old path's error contract (here, no failing read after a committed write).

evidence: ApplyUpdateInput.Fields is UpdateIssueInput, which still has Status, and IsEmpty even checks u.Status. A caller setting Fields.Status gets the transitions applied and then a rejection in UpdateIssue, leaving a partial update. The right cure is a field type with no Status, not a runtime guard.
guidance_note: When a new input type routes one field elsewhere, give it a struct that cannot carry that field instead of reusing the old input wholesale.

evidence: The refactor's point is sequencing status and fields in one call, and the reviewer notes update_test.go covers only status-only and field-only. The packet shows no combined test added, and the PR merged before the review.
guidance_note: When a refactor merges two code paths, add a test that exercises both at once.

evidence: `if normalizedTarget != "" && normalizedTarget != in.TargetStatus` discards an empty normalization, so whitespace TargetStatus reaches statusTransitionActionsForApplyUpdate unnormalized, contradicting the 'empty TargetStatus = no transitions' doc. The adjacent `_ = current` dead line was later removed in #99, but not this.
guidance_note: Assign a normalizer's result unconditionally instead of guarding the write-back on non-empty.

narrative: The PR was merged six minutes after creation, nineteen seconds before Copilot's review posted. All four findings (a write-then-read error path, a type that admits the wrong field, a missing combined test, and a dropped normalization) went unanswered. Each is real.
guidance_observations: The PR merged before the reviewer finished; merging should wait for the review to post and every thread to be answered.
Four substantive findings on merged code were never routed to a ticket.

evidence: The diff renamed runWithWorkspace's param to `_ []string` and left runWithApp's commandArgs unused after deleting enforceBeadsPreflight; the agent dropped the param and its construction in e49b55c.
guidance_note: When deleting the last use of a parameter, delete the parameter and its call-site construction instead of blanking it to `_`.

evidence: The hunk shows the sync CommandSpec line flush-left after the migrate entry was deleted, which is gofmt drift; fixed in e49b55c.
guidance_note: Run gofmt on every touched Go file before pushing.

evidence: The exit_test.go table row is flush-left after the deleted beads row, the same gofmt drift as F2; fixed in e49b55c.
guidance_note: Run gofmt on every touched Go file before pushing.

narrative: Deletion PR with one round of three findings: a dead parameter and two gofmt slips from line-level deletions. All were fixed in e49b55c. Nothing fix-caused.
guidance_observations: Two of three findings were gofmt drift that a pre-push gofmt run would have removed.

evidence: The reply-hint says accept, but the reply 'session id is the correct value' is a pushback. The placeholder tells agents what to put in the assignee value, a deliberate convention, and the CLI flag's '<user>' label does not constrain the value type.

`lit rank <id> [--top] [--bottom] [--above <other-id>] [--below <other-id>]` marks every mode as optional, while the CLI requires exactly one. An agent following it literally can run a bare `lit rank <id>` and error. `(--top|--bottom|--above <id>|--below <id>)` costs no extra length.
guidance_note: In usage lines, write mutually exclusive required flags as (a|b|c), not as independent [a] [b] [c].

narrative: Quickstart pruning PR, one round. The assignee placeholder finding misread a deliberate convention and was rightly refused. The rank-syntax finding was correct and cheap to fix, but it was dismissed.

evidence: The bash command list in the hunk has no followup, next, orphaned, or import, all registered commands (orphaned was added in #85 and followup in #90). The PR was closed as a duplicate of #97/#98 and the drift was never ticketed.
guidance_note: When registering a new top-level command, update the completion scripts in the same PR, or generate completions from commandSpecs.

evidence: The zsh list has the same drift as F1, a hand-maintained copy of the command registry missing the same four commands; it went unanswered when the PR closed.
guidance_note: When registering a new top-level command, update the completion scripts in the same PR, or generate completions from commandSpecs.

evidence: The fish subcommand string in the hunk likewise lacks followup, next, orphaned, and import; it went unanswered when the PR closed.
guidance_note: When registering a new top-level command, update the completion scripts in the same PR, or generate completions from commandSpecs.

narrative: This was a duplicate of the #97 sunset PR, closed as already merged. Its one round surfaced real completion-list drift across bash, zsh, and fish, accumulated from earlier PRs that added commands without touching completion.go. None of it was answered or ticketed.
guidance_observations: Real findings on a PR closed as duplicate were dropped; they apply to master and should have become a ticket.
Three hand-maintained copies of the command list drift from commandSpecs, a one-source-of-truth gap no single PR was asked to sweep.
